meta.oneLiner: A stalled competitive displacement, restarted by finding the real economic buyer.

stakeholders.name: Dana Okafor
stakeholders.title: CFO
stakeholders.note: Owns the number. Cared about audit risk, not features.

stakeholders.name: Marcus Hale
stakeholders.title: VP Finance
stakeholders.note: Built the business case with me. Sold internally when I couldn't.

stakeholders.name: Priya Raman
stakeholders.title: Controller
stakeholders.note: Fed me the close-process pain, week by week.

stakeholders.name: Tom Byrne
stakeholders.title: CISO
stakeholders.note: Hard no until SOC 2 scope and SSO were proven.

stakeholders.name: Lena Cruz
stakeholders.title: VP Field Operations
stakeholders.note: 2,400 drivers on paper receipts. Loudest advocate.

stakeholders.name: Gil Anders
stakeholders.title: Dir. Procurement
stakeholders.note: Incumbent relationship. Ran the process to protect it.

stakeholders.name: Ava Sterling
stakeholders.title: Assoc. General Counsel
stakeholders.note: DPA and liability cap. Two weeks of the cycle.

obstacles.title: Six-year incumbent
obstacles.resolution: Reframed on audit findings, not price.

obstacles.title: Champion went quiet
obstacles.detail: Reorg moved my champion off the project.
obstacles.resolution: Re-anchored on the CFO's board commitment.

obstacles.title: Security review
obstacles.detail: CISO blocked pending SOC 2 scope + SCIM.
obstacles.resolution: Ran a joint architecture session in week 9.

obstacles.title: NetSuite integration
obstacles.resolution: Scoped a 3-week pilot on one subsidiary.

obstacles.title: No budget line
obstacles.detail: Spend sat inside three cost centers.

obstacles.title: Liability cap standoff
obstacles.detail: Legal wanted 3x fees; we cap at 1x.
obstacles.resolution: Traded cap for a shorter cure period.

economicBuyer.headline: CFO, met in week 6
economicBuyer.proof: Board had committed to a clean FY26 audit.

decisionCriteria.headline: Audit trail over features
decisionCriteria.proof: We wrote the criteria with the Controller.

decisionProcess.headline: Security → Legal → CFO sign-off
decisionProcess.proof: Mapped in week 7. Legal was the hidden gate.

paperProcess.headline: DPA + 3-week security review
paperProcess.proof: Started legal in parallel, not after.

identifyPain.headline: Failed audit control
identifyPain.proof: Two repeat findings on expense approvals.

champion.headline: VP Finance, tested twice
champion.proof: He ran the internal readout without me.

steps.title: A locked-in incumbent
steps.notes: Set the table fast. This is a displacement, not a greenfield deal.

steps.title: An audit finding, twice
steps.notes: The Controller gave me the number. Numbers travel; adjectives don't.

steps.title: Then it went dark
bullets: Reorg pulled my champion off the project
steps.notes: Own the miss out loud: I had a champion, not an economic buyer.

steps.title: Found the real buyer
bullets: CFO had committed the board to a clean audit
Traded a features pitch for a risk conversation
Funded from audit remediation, not IT budget
steps.notes: This is the hinge of the story. Slow down here.

steps.title: Two gates, in parallel
bullets: SOC 2 scope and SCIM cleared the CISO
Pilot scoped to one subsidiary, three weeks
steps.notes: Parallel, not sequential. That's where the 31 days came from.

steps.title: Legal was the real gate
bullets: Started the DPA in week 7, not week 20
Traded liability cap for a shorter cure period
steps.notes: Most reps discover legal in week 20. Name that contrast.

steps.title: $1.24M, 187 days
steps.notes: Land the number, then stop talking.

steps.title: Pain travels upward
bullets: Qualify the buyer, not the meeting
Run security and legal in parallel
A champion you haven't tested isn't one
steps.notes: Close on the transferable lesson — that's what they're hiring.
